jo-01-verbo-sinais.context: John presents Jesus as the Word who became flesh. In this passage, many reject him, but whoever receives him and believes in his name becomes a child of God and receives grace upon grace.
jo-01-verbo-sinais.focusQuestion: What changes for you in knowing that God became flesh and dwelt among us?
jo-01-verbo-sinais.keywordGloss: The name John gives Jesus in this chapter, the Son who was with God and became flesh.
facts: Jesus came to what was his own, but his own did not receive him.
Whoever receives Jesus and believes in his name becomes a child of God.
God's children are born of God, not of human will.
The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.
All received from Jesus' fullness, grace upon grace.
Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

jo-02-eu-sou.context: Jesus is about to leave and comforts the disciples by speaking of the place he will prepare. Thomas and Philip ask questions, and Jesus shows that knowing him is knowing the Father.
jo-02-eu-sou.focusQuestion: When you don't know which way to go, what changes as you look to Jesus?
jo-02-eu-sou.keywordGloss: The word with which Jesus presents himself to Thomas, the way to the Father.
facts: Jesus will return to receive the disciples to himself.
Thomas says he does not know where Jesus is going.
Jesus presents himself as the way, the truth and the life.
No one comes to the Father except through Jesus.
Philip asks Jesus to show them the Father.
Whoever sees Jesus also sees the Father.

jo-03-adeus-espirito.context: In his farewell, Jesus compares the disciples' life to branches joined to a vine. Without remaining in him, the branch bears no fruit; joined to him, it bears much fruit and glorifies the Father.
jo-03-adeus-espirito.focusQuestion: In what area of your life do you need to stay joined to Jesus today?
jo-03-adeus-espirito.keywordGloss: Staying joined to Jesus continually, as the branch remains in the vine.
facts: The branch that bears no fruit is cut off, and the one that does is pruned.
The branch cannot bear fruit by itself.
Whoever remains in Jesus bears much fruit.
Without Jesus, the disciples can do nothing.
If Jesus' words remain in them, they will ask and receive.
The Father is glorified when the disciples bear much fruit.

jo-04-cruz-tome.context: On the cross, Jesus cares for his mother, says he is thirsty so that Scripture is fulfilled, and declares his work finished. Already dead, his legs are not broken by the soldiers.
jo-04-cruz-tome.focusQuestion: What do you need to entrust to Jesus, believing that his work is complete?
jo-04-cruz-tome.keywordGloss: Jesus' word on the cross as he gave up his life with the work fulfilled.
facts: The disciple takes Jesus' mother into his own home.
Jesus says he is thirsty after seeing that all was finished.
They soaked a sponge in sour wine and brought it to Jesus' mouth.
Jesus declares that it is finished and gives up his spirit.
The bodies were not to stay on the cross during the Sabbath.
The soldiers do not break the legs of Jesus, already dead.

jo-boss-revisao.context: This challenge reviews John, from the Word made flesh to the finished cross. Jesus reveals himself as the way and the vine, and calls the reader to believe in him and remain in him.
jo-boss-revisao.focusQuestion: In light of all John has shown, what does believing in Jesus mean to you?
jo-boss-revisao.keywordGloss: The name John gives Jesus, the Son who became flesh and dwelt among us.
facts: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.
Whoever receives Jesus and believes in his name becomes a child of God.
Jesus presents himself as the way, the truth and the life.
Whoever remains in Jesus bears much fruit.
Without Jesus, the disciples can do nothing.
Jesus declares that it is finished and gives up his spirit.
